selection.rule: Dependency-complete first 24 questions from the question-sheet selection order.

questions.question: What scene are readers told to imagine at the beginning of the passage?
questions.answer: They are told to picture a time of deep ignorance and harsh living, when people saw the world as lifeless and covered by heedlessness.

questions.question: What are the Qur’an’s verses compared to in the passage?
questions.answer: They are compared to bright stars.

questions.question: What happens in the minds of listeners when they hear that everything in the heavens and earth praises Allah?
questions.answer: They begin to see creatures as alive, awake, and engaged in remembering Allah.

questions.question: What does hearing that all things glorify Allah cause people to notice?
questions.answer: It causes them to notice that all creatures carry meaning and worship their Lord.

questions.question: In the image given, what do the stars become for the listener?
questions.answer: They become shining signs that speak wisdom and truth.

questions.question: How is the earth presented in that same scene?
questions.answer: It is presented like a head, with its parts acting like tongues of praise.

questions.question: What is one major lesson of the star comparison for the verses?
questions.answer: Each verse spreads light into darkness, like stars shining in the night.

questions.question: What is the problem with looking through a “veil of familiarity”?
questions.answer: It makes a person careless and keeps them from noticing the freshness and power of the message.

questions.question: What is the main purpose of the examples of sky, stars, earth, animals, and plants?
questions.answer: They show how the Qur’an teaches people to see all creation as pointing to Allah.

questions.question: What does the passage say comes next for someone who wants deeper understanding?
questions.answer: A comparison that explains one of the loftiest levels of the Qur’an’s miraculousness.

questions.question: What kind of darkness is mentioned in the opening of the passage?
questions.answer: It speaks of the darkness of unbelief, ignorance, and heedlessness.

questions.question: How are the Qur’an’s verses described in relation to disbelief?
questions.answer: They are described as lights that break apart its darkness.

questions.question: What effect do the Qur’an’s verses have on that mistaken worldview?
questions.answer: They tear it apart and replace it with a vision of a living creation connected to Allah.

questions.question: After the verse about glorification is heard, what happens to the way creatures are understood?
questions.answer: They are understood as living signs that remember and praise Allah.

questions.question: How is the sky presented to the listener after hearing the verse about glorification?
questions.answer: It is presented like a speaking mouth filled with meaningful, shining signs.

questions.question: What does the passage say happens when people only see these verses as already well-known religious truths?
questions.answer: They miss how powerfully each verse first broke through darkness and may not taste its miraculous sweetness.

questions.question: Why does the passage tell readers to imagine an earlier age instead of just thinking from their own time?
questions.answer: Because seeing the first setting helps them notice the powerful change the Qur’an brought.

questions.question: What overall transformation does the passage show from before the Qur’an to after it?
questions.answer: It shows a change from a dead and dark view of the world to a living and faith-filled view.

questions.question: What kind of appreciation does the passage want from the reader?
questions.answer: It wants thoughtful, heartfelt appreciation of the Qur’an’s guidance and miraculous power.

questions.question: Why does the passage end by mentioning a coming comparison?
questions.answer: To lead the reader into a fuller explanation of a very high form of the Qur’an’s miraculousness.

questions.question: What kind of world are readers asked to picture before the Qur’an’s light appears?
questions.answer: A world filled with ignorance, roughness, and a belief that things are lifeless and without meaning.

questions.question: What was the mistaken way of seeing the world in that imagined age?
questions.answer: People saw things as dead, ruled only by nature, and covered by ignorance.

questions.question: What mental picture are readers invited to enter before hearing the example verses?
questions.answer: They are invited to imagine a society buried in ignorance, heedlessness, and a lifeless view of creation.

questions.question: How are the verses of the Qur’an pictured in the first sentence of the passage?
questions.answer: They are pictured like brilliant stars spreading light.

title: Reviving Effect of Verses in the Age of Ignorance
